Jeffrey St. Clair recently stated in
[_CounterPunch_](https://www.counterpunch.org/2026/03/02/notes-on-iran/) that
“Iran’s leadership was discussing a plan to end its enriched uranium program
when [the February 28th] attack was launched.” The U.S. bombing “was a joint
venture with Israel,” stated St. Clair, “which has never wanted negotiations
with Iran, only an end to the regime.” [Stephen
Zunes](https://stephenzunes.org/) remarked just after the attack that “an
[Omani
mediator](https://www.lemonde.fr/en/international/article/2026/02/28/mediator-
oman-hails-breakthrough-in-us-iran-nuclear-talks_6750947_4.html) said a
nuclear agreement with Iran was within reach [and] in response, the United
States and Israel started bombing.”

Further, [Lawrence Davidson](https://www.counterpunch.org/author/lawrence-
davidson/) indicated that “Iran had agreed to deactivate its [uranium
stockpile](https://thehill.com/policy/international/5759623-iran-nuclear-deal-
stockpiling/). This done, it could not create a bomb. It is exactly the moment
that the Iranians agreed to this that Trump and Netanyahu decided to launch
their attack.” [Trita Parsi](https://x.com/tparsi?lang=en) at the [Quincy
Institute for Responsible Statecraft](https://quincyinst.org/author/trita-
parsi/) verifies a similar claim.

[Sinan Ulgen](https://carnegieendowment.org/people/sinan-ulgen), a former
Turkish diplomat said, “the moral dilemma that we are all facing as neighbors
of Iran on this first day, of what is likely to be a protracted regional
escalation, is about defending multilateral norms vs. nuclear proliferation.”
“The U.S. attacks are from an international law perspective,” said
[Ulgen](https://x.com/sinanulgen1/status/2027790100487082082), “totally
[illegal](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/3/3/are-us-israeli-attacks-
against-iran-legal-under-international-law) and illegitimate, but now that the
campaign has started, Iran’s political will and nuclear infrastructure emerge
relatively unscathed from all of this. The next phase will surely be regional
proliferation.” Lebanese journalist [Kim Ghattas](https://x.com/KimGhattas)
called Trump’s actions “the ultimate hubris, a president more focused on the
spectacle of power than its consequences.”

**Events and Facts**

Leading up to the war, as for the death toll among the [2025-2026 Iranian
protesters](https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/jan/27/iran-
protests-death-toll-disappeared-bodies-mass-burials-30000-dead) in 27 of its
31 provinces, the Human Rights Activists News Agency ([HRANA](https://www.en-
hrana.org/)), [Amnesty
International](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/campaigns/2026/01/what-
happened-at-the-protests-in-iran/), and [Human Rights
Watch](https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/01/16/iran-growing-evidence-of-
countrywide-massacres) estimated the number to be around 6,000 while a number
of 33,000 spread on social media and among right-leaning diasporic sources
without verification. The larger figure conflates historical prison executions
dating back to [1988](https://www.hrw.org/news/2022/06/08/irans-1988-mass-
executions), is impacted by internet blackout, and politically motivated.

Additionally, actors such as the [People’s Mojahedin Organization of Iran
(MEK)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/People%27s_Mojahedin_Organization_of_Iran),
may have intentionally inflated the numbers. Further, there have been reports
that political violence in Tehran extends to leftists found and [killed by
Mossad](https://www.thecanary.co/skwawkbox/2026/03/01/us-and-israel-accused-
of-targeting-left-wing-activists-in-iran/). These facts illustrate a gap
between irresponsibly circulated statements by Trump apologists and the actual
verifiable evidence. What is more, Trump and Netanyahu’s poorly handled public
statements months prior to the war, signaled the Iranian Revolutionary Guard
Corps to hunt down U.S. and Israeli recruited Iranian soldiers (610,000 active
personnel,) according to [Seymour
Hersh](https://seymourhersh.substack.com/p/is-trump-a-liability-in-his-own-
war).

Overall, [U.S. intelligence](https://m.economictimes.com/news/defence/us-
intel-did-not-suggest-a-preemptive-strike-from-iran-before-us-israeli-attack-
ap-sources-say/amp_articleshow/128934510.cms) found no proof of an imminent
Iranian threat although the
[UN](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2025/aug/27/return-of-un-nuclear-
inspectors-to-iran-met-with-protests-by-mps) could not verify a complete
[suspension of uranium](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/world/un-nuclear-
watchdog-says-its-unable-to-verify-whether-iran-has-suspended-all-uranium-
enrichment). On March 3, it was reported by Iranian authorities that at least
168-180 people, including many school children, were killed in Minab by an
airstrike. The girls’ school, [Shajareh Tayyebeh
Elementary](https://www.nbcnews.com/world/iran/know-strike-school-iran-death-
toll-rises-rcna261266), was originally built near a military base but the base
has been closed for 15 years. Videos showing the Islamic Republic using
civilians as human shields have been debunked as AI generated by
[FactNameh](https://factnameh.com/fa/fact-checks/2026-03-03-iran-use-
prisoners-as-human-shield-video-fake) and the theory of Iranian misfire lacks
forensic and operational proof.

Other anecdotal and unverified reports of the [human shield
narrative](https://www.iranintl.com/202603046637) lack supporting evidence.
Additionally, [satellite
imagery](https://www.opb.org/article/2026/03/04/satellite-images-suggests-
airstrike-destroyed-iranian-school/) reported by
[NPR](https://www.npr.org/2026/03/04/nx-s1-5735801/satellite-imagery-shows-
strike-that-destroyed-iranian-school-was-more-extensive-than-first-reported)
reveals that initial airstrikes on Iran featured multiple targets. The imagery
is inconsistent with what would amount to Iranian friendly fire. [Later
analysis](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/05/world/middleeast/iran-school-us-
strikes-naval-base.html) reveals it was likely a U.S. strike. Zunes, commented
that “schools, hospitals, city parks, and cultural sites are being targeted in
the United States and Israeli bombing of Tehran.” This included the [Azadi
Sports Stadium](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/03/06/world/middleeast/iran-
strikes-azadi-stadium.html).

**Interpretations and Motives**

The 2026 Iran War features a larger fragmentation of the [American ruling
class](https://jacobin.com/2021/04/take-me-to-your-leader-the-rot-of-the-
american-ruling-class). Trump is having a difficult time
[rationalizing](https://slate.com/news-and-politics/2026/03/trump-plan-iran-
war.html?pay=1772684092918&support_journalism=please) and finding his
rhetorical bearings with an unpopular action that suddenly has involved 16
nations [and counting](https://www.channel4.com/news/are-we-on-the-cusp-of-an-
iran-ground-offensive). Aside from the international consensus and clear
violations of IHL and global norms, Trump has violated customary human rights
obligations and standard foreign policy practices found in [Just War
Theory](https://firstthings.com/just-war-theory-and-operation-epic-fury/),
[realism](https://www.theamericanconservative.com/war-on-iran-is-the-opposite-
of-realism/), and the doctrines of [smart
power](https://time.com/7382278/iran-bombing-regime-change-pape/). As the
[U.S. Senate fails](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/3/5/iran-
live-us-senate-backs-trumps-attacks-on-tehran-israel-pounds-lebanon) to “[curb
Trump’s war powers](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/3/4/iran-
live-news-us-embassy-in-dubai-hit-israel-pounds-tehran-
beirut#:~:text=%E2%81%A0A%20%E2%81%A0majority%20of,accuses%20EU%20of%20'double%20standards'),”
the president ignores “the [lessons of
Iraq](https://www.cfr.org/articles/trumps-iran-campaign-ignores-the-lessons-
of-the-iraq-war).” And as Harvard’s [Steven
Levitsky](https://www.gov.harvard.edu/directory/steven-levitsky/) once noted,
“state failure brings violence and instability; it almost never brings
[democratization](https://www.journalofdemocracy.org/articles/the-myth-of-
democratic-recession/).”

The Joint Chief of Staff Chairman [Gen. Dan
Caine](https://www.jcs.mil/Leadership/Article-View/Article/1974872/gen-dan-
caine/) has been [concerned with the plan](https://apnews.com/article/trump-
iran-maga-regime-change-2758513ac034ffb75beaa12db68c7bd7) and warned of its
potential challenges. Trump’s policy of “[Maximum

**America’s War of Choice**

In 2009, Council on Foreign Relations President [Richard
Haass](https://www.cfr.org/experts/richard-haass) authored, [_War of
Necessity, War of Choice: A Memoir of Two Iraq
Wars_](https://www.brookings.edu/events/war-of-necessity-war-of-choice/) _._
He compared the first war’s (1991) “traditional, legitimate, and strategic”
approach to the second war (2003) — one “poorly conceived and implemented.”
Haass concluded that “using force to oust regimes is simply too costly and too
uncertain.” [David E. Sanger](https://www.nytimes.com/by/david-e-sanger),
recently in the [_New York
Times_](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/02/28/us/politics/trump-iran-attack.html)
stated, “For Trump, the Iran Attack Is the Ultimate War of Choice.” Sanger
remarked that Trump “was not driven by an immediate threat” and did not
present evidence to justify the [action](https://jinsa.org/wp-
content/uploads/2026/03/Operations-Epic-Fury-and-Roaring-Lion-03-01-26.pdf).
The concept of [necessity in war](https://www.ncronline.org/news/congress-
expected-consider-war-powers-resolution-after-us-israel-strikes-iran) requires
the use of force only as a last resort.

Senior Policy Director at the European Council on Foreign Relations [Jeremy
Cliffe](https://ecfr.eu/profile/jeremy-cliffe/) stated that “Europeans should
communicate clearly that this is a war of choice by America, in contravention
of the same UN charter [they] have invoked to condemn Russia’s illegal
invasion of Ukraine and insist on Greenland’s sovereignty.” This conflict
however, looks to be [Israel’s war of
necessity](https://campuscore.ariel.ac.il/wp/mecarc/israels-war-of-
necessity/).

[Operation Epic Fury](https://jinsa.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/03/Operations-
Epic-Fury-and-Roaring-Lion-03-02-26-1.pdf) presents a preventative strike, not
a [preemptive](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c5yj9kr31y7o) one under
international law, much like Russia’s decision to invade Ukraine, which was
denounced as a clear violation of international norms. [Stephen
Zunes](https://www.usfca.edu/faculty/stephen-zunes) pointed out, “This is not
a preemptive war. A preemptive war is in response to an imminent attack. This
is a war of aggression. A flagrant violation of the United Nations Charter.”
Alarmingly, Trump stated over a month before the invasion that “[I don’t need
international law](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/01/08/us/politics/trump-
interview-power-morality.html),” as he currently creates [new
norms](https://www.chathamhouse.org/2026/03/iran-attacks-president-trump-
making-use-force-new-normal-and-casting-aside-international). Zunes previously
stated that “this war isn’t about nonproliferation, it’s about inflicting as
much damage as possible on a country that isn’t willing to accept U.S.
hegemony in the region.”

Overall, since returning to office for a second term, the Trump administration
has carried out air strikes in Venezuela, Nigeria, Syria, Iraq, Iran, Yemen,
and Somalia, according to the [Council on Foreign
Relations](https://www.cfr.org/articles/guide-trumps-second-term-military-
strikes-and-actions). In the Iran 2026 War, the U.S. has already carried out
over [3,000 strikes](https://www.wsj.com/livecoverage/iran-war-news-
updates-2026/card/u-s-central-command-1-000-strikes-on-iran-in-three-
days-K2lwsvAMvwleklEilYTA?gaa_at=eafs&gaa_n=AWEtsqeKRUf1T2NWYyMn7AYU_lTP2WrhQU6jq80qOuvUkJaD9yT6YxbdvB3c4dx90kY%3D&gaa_ts=69ac865b&gaa_sig=rIAAmjIYg2Mn3_9whPyPbj-
CADwIV0n-NfWST15LVcTE7NjR9q0YMfG45Gzwf_WjV8RYrGH4dpPdkL96BXBkTQ%3D%3D).

Sanger emphasized however, that “Netanyahu urged [Trump] starting in
[December](https://www.timesofisrael.com/liveblog_entry/netanyahu-trump-began-
planning-for-joint-strike-on-iran-in-december-report/) to launch this war”
with little plan in sight. There is mounting evidence that [interests serve
Israel](https://newlinesmag.com/running-notes/israel-cant-maintain-a-long-war-
with-iran-and-the-us-isnt-interested/) much more than the U.S. Top aides,
diplomats, its [top general](https://www.axios.com/2026/02/23/iran-strike-
trump-gen-dan-caine-vance-rubio), and the [American
people](https://www.ipsos.com/en-us/more-americans-disapprove-approve-us-
strikes-against-iran), have little faith in the attacks. America’s closest
friend, [Britain](https://www.ejiltalk.org/the-legality-of-the-uk-
interception-of-iranian-missiles-and-permitting-a-limited-us-use-of-british-
bases/), refused the American military’s access to the [Diego
Garcia](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/mar/02/uk-airbases-us-attack-
iran-trump-starmer) to launch American fighter jets. This later shifted to
limited use.

**Israel’s War of Necessity**

It appears that the U.S. is clearly acting on behalf of Israel and prefers to
use the country as an excuse to mobilize and cloud a series of [domestic
issues](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c1d66k5r1x4o) impacting Trump’s
unpopularity [at home](https://truthout.org/articles/new-report-indicates-
trump-linked-epstein-records-kept-out-of-doj-database/). Ulgen also advanced
that Trump “wanted to enter the November midterm elections as the U.S. leader
who overthrew the regime in Iran.” A recent
[_Politico_](https://www.politico.com/news/2026/02/25/white-house-politics-
israel-strikes-iran-00799456) article stated that “White House Officials
believe ‘the politics are a lot better’ if Israel strikes Iran first.”

The question remains, how this decision impacts U.S. strategic interests.
Muhammad Idrees Ahmad of [_New Lines Magazine_](https://newlinesmag.com/)
indicated that the U.S. has no motive to go to war with Iran except for Israel
and they have been pushing for a U.S. attack for the last 30 years. After
September 11, 2001, the neocons targeted Iraq “only because it was part of
their ‘[dual rollback](https://newlinesmag.com/argument/the-uses-and-abuses-
of-the-iraq-war/)’ policy [and] selling a war on Iran seemed less achievable,”
cited Ahmad. All the while Trump’s philosophical departures from Bolton, Bush
and Cheney seem exaggerated and he’s like other hard-right hawks.

Netanyahu, “a wanted war criminal,” says reporter [Secunder
Kermani](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/uk-journalist-confronts-israeli-
spokesman-191245015.html?guccounter=1&guce_referrer=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZ29vZ2xlLmNvbS8&guce_referrer_sig=AQAAAHPKk-
TU-3RZWp8-KKivmxiXIoiBIx0D_fWZjPucwl0WyoPLc3_15L9mIVzALPUIFH5Q-UKlek1Ts24KUhpwOvEZMgaQtQ1QKD5gEpEzqQl9Qd9HupzsacXi_omUKJ3TFJXbyDOGE1bHjipAWLrv9gx26PMaEaFhm3hyCORuzk7Y),

iran-is-being-pushed-toward-state-collapse/) _._ Trump lacks support from

Claiming that Israel has “[a free
hand](https://www.politico.com/newsletters/national-security-
daily/2025/08/21/trump-increasingly-gives-bibi-a-free-hand-00518529)” and
drives U.S. foreign policy is usually a problematic accusation for many

stated](https://www.israelnationalnews.com/news/423182), “Israel now has the
assistance of the United States, my friend, U.S. President Donald Trump, and
the U.S. military. This coalition of forces allows us to do what I have
yearned to do for 40 years.” Iran is a thorn in the side of the U.S. but a
major juggernaut for Israel.

For the most part, the U.S. has avoided the use of regional hard power when it
came to the Iranian government. It seemed to go along with the Iranian foreign
policy, what analyst [Mouin Rabbani](https://x.com/MouinRabbani) referred to

analysis/strategic-patience-and-irans-resistance-axis-enduring-challenge-
bidens).” All the while, the U.S. has implemented a host of structural and
cultural impediments to Iran’s social and political development including the
toppling of democratically elected
[Mosaddegh](https://www.cia.gov/readingroom/docs/the%20central%20intelligence%20%5B15369853%5D.pdf)
in [1953](https://www.zinnedproject.org/news/tdih/iran-coup/), unlawful

Although it was argued that George W. Bush allowed Israel to fly
